data.title: Wall Street Journal editorial board knocks Hegseth's 'weirdos' line in speech
data.description:
The Wall Street Journal’s conservative editorial board on Friday criticized Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s fiery comment during a Wednesday speech to active-duty officers that he wants “warriors” not “weirdos” in the military.

While the opinion piece praised new initiatives introduced by the secretary during this address, including the development of autonomous warfare technology and partnering with universities for officer recruitment, the board expressed concern that Hegseth’s “gratuitous potshots” could negatively impact recruitment efforts. 

“Alas, Mr. Hegseth couldn’t resist his usual polarizing attack routine against all and sundry, and he even accused the press of ‘treason’ for publishing what’s leaking out of the secretary’s shop,” the board wrote. 

“The most remembered line of the speech will be Mr. Hegseth’s declaration that the U.S. military no longer abides ‘beardos’ or ‘weirdos,’” the opinion continued. “As a practical matter, has he met anyone in defense technology lately?”

During his Wednesday speech, Hegseth revived culture-war grievances and declared the Pentagon is “no longer the woke department or the weak department.”

“Simple translation of that: No fatties, no t——, no beardos, no weirdos, no wimps, no radicals. Just warriors,” Hegseth continued, using a pejorative term for transgender individuals. 

Alyssa Farah Griffin, a co-host of “The View” and former special assistant to President Trump, said during a Friday show she thought Hegseth’s comment was “a parody” when she first saw it posted online.

“We are the greatest fighting force in the history of mankind,” Griffin said. “We’re not weak, we’re not incapable and I don’t know where he’s hearing this from.”

Griffin called the speech “bizarre” and referenced a new Republican-led effort to remove Hegseth from his role. Last month, GOP Rep. Thomas Massie (Ky.) introduced an impeachment resolution against the secretary, citing the U.S.’s ongoing military operations against Iran. 

Some Republican lawmakers, including Massie, have become increasingly more outspoken against these operations as the conflict stretches into an eighth month. The House has passed three Iran war powers resolutions with the support of several Republicans, and the Senate approved a similar measure in June.

data.title: President Trump has his camera off for G7 leader zoom
data.description:
President Trump participated in a video-call meeting with leaders of the Group of Seven (G7) countries and the International Energy Agency (IEA) on Friday, but his camera was off while other leaders appeared on camera. 

Fatih Birol, executive director of the IEA, said in a post on the social platform X that leaders met to discuss the global energy market and “severe pressures” on diesel supply. Birol attached a photo of the virtual meeting that showed leaders of Canada, Germany, Italy, the United Kingdom, the European Commission, France and Japan on camera while Trump was not. 

It is not clear if the president’s camera was off for the entire meeting or just at the moment the picture was taken. 

Birol attached a statement from the G7 leaders in which they acknowledged the volatility in oil markets and “surging prices threatening economic stability.” Diesel costs are up by more than $2 compared with a year ago, while gasoline is up by more than a dollar.

The statement said the G7 member countries, which include the U.S., would be releasing 100 million barrels of oil over the next four months with a substantial diesel release in the first 20 days. The statement condemned Iran for disrupting international trade and energy security and applauded the U.S.

“We have agreed on decisive, coordinated measures to stabilize immediate energy supplies, shield households and businesses from price shocks, and strengthen the long-term resilience of global energy systems,” the statement read. 

“We commend the United States for its efforts to ensure the free flow of commerce through the strait of Hormuz,” it added.

Trump said in a post to Truth social Friday morning that Europe had agreed to immediately release a “massive amount” of their diesel stockpile.

Trump has repeatedly downplayed the concerns over rising oil and gas costs and said last month that the price bump is a “very inexpensive price to pay” for what has occurred in the Iran war.

data.title: Trump's motorcade neared 100 mph en route to Oklahoma after helicopter, airplane ruled out
data.description:
President Trump’s motorcade put the pedal to the metal Thursday as stormy weather in the South spurred the president to drive from rallies in Texas to Oklahoma rather than fly.

Trump took the motorcade from his event at the Peterbilt Motors manufacturing plant in Denton, Texas to his second event in Durant, Oklahoma. The locations are roughly 90 miles apart. Press travelling with the president noted that the vans reached speeds of 98 mph.

Typically, the president would’ve taken Marine One from Texas to Oklahoma, but stormy weather spurred the last-minute decision to drive.

During the ride to Oklahoma, Trump posted on social media that the Beast, or the car the president rides in, was going “faster than it has ever gone before.”

“To the Great People of Oklahoma, stay tuned — I’ll be there soon! There was a major weather delay, and the planes and helicopters were not able to land, so we’re driving up from Texas,” he wrote on Truth Social. “They wanted me to postpone the event, and I said, ‘NO WAY, I’M GOING TO OKLAHOMA!’ ‘The Beast’ is going faster than it has ever gone before. It won’t be long. I love you all! See you in a little while.”

Trump showed up about two hours late in Durant, telling the crowd that he refused to cancel it entirely.

“I said, ‘What can I take?’” he told the crowd.

“I said, ‘How fast does the Beast travel?’ They said, ‘We could go close to a 100 miles per hour,’” he continued. “I said, ‘Get your asses in that car. We’re going to Oklahoma.”

Trump said he wanted to make sure he made it to Oklahoma, not because the candidates needed his help, but because he won the state all three times he ran for president.

“We got the most votes ever in the state history all three times,” he said. “And we won all 77 out of 77 counties.”

data.title: Republican super PAC shifts money from North Carolina to Kansas
data.description:
The Senate Leadership Fund (SLF), a Republican PAC that raises money and spends on ads supporting GOP Senate candidates, is moving money out of North Carolina and into Kansas, according to a source familiar with SLF’s plans.

The move is a sign that the Kansas race is growing more competitive for Democrats, as polls suggest the GOP’s chances of winning in North Carolina are narrowing. 

The PAC is pausing its $30 million advertising campaign in support of Michael Whatley, former Republican National Committee chair, in North Carolina amid his tight race with Democratic former Gov. Roy Cooper.

Cooper is favored to win, according to elections analysts, and one recent poll had him 11 points ahead.

The change was first reported by Semafor.

The race in Kansas, usually a safe Republican seat in the Senate, has tightened in recent weeks as Democratic candidate Adam Hamilton, founding pastor of one of the state’s largest churches, emerged from the primary field and has garnered attention and money, while taking aim at incumbent Sen. Roger Marshall’s (R) support for the unpopular Iran war and other Trump administration policies.

Elections analysts shifted that race slightly more in Democrats’ favor last month, though Marshall is still seen as the favorite. 

According to AdImpact, a website that tracks advertising spending in politics, the SLF has reserved $485,000 so far for the Kansas Senate race, and ads are set to begin next week. One ad against Hamilton, released Friday morning, calls him a “two-faced extremist,” pushing against Hamilton’s narrative that he is politically moderate. 

The SLF has also recently put more money into Midwest states like Iowa and Ohio, which were once expected to be safer for Republican candidates but now face similar challenges as Kansas.

data.title: Amazon investing $1B in data center communities
data.description:
Amazon plans to invest $1 billion in communities where it builds data centers over the next five years, the company announced Friday.

The e-commerce and cloud computing giant will put the funds toward free community college and workforce training for residents, as well as energy efficiency upgrades.

“We understand why there is apprehension in some communities where data centers are being built,” Amazon Web Services (AWS) CEO Matt Garman wrote in a blog post.

“While there is much we (and other data center operators) are already doing, we’ve decided to codify our practices into a series of tenets that we’re calling our ‘Amazon Data Center Commitment,'” he added.

The firm said it will ensure the facilities don’t raise residents’ electricity bills and pledged to no longer use nondisclosure agreements (NDAs).

Amazon is also aiming to make its data centers “water positive” by 2030, meaning they would return more water to the system than they use. It intends to annually publish information about water usage and efficiency, as well as energy usage and efficiency.

The new commitments come as data centers have become increasingly unpopular, complicating the push to rapidly build more of the server warehouses across the country to support AI development.

A recent poll from Pew Research Center found that 60 percent of Americans would be uncomfortable with a data center operating in their area.

Central to the backlash are concerns about the impact on energy costs and the environment. Half of those in the Pew survey said data centers were mostly bad for home energy costs, while 54 percent said they were mostly bad for the environment.

Garman suggested Friday that some of the pushback is misinformed, arguing that allegations data centers are “taking all of our water” or are “responsible for driving up all the energy rates” are false or misleading.

“There is urgency to this data center buildout because we aren’t the only country that sees the benefits of AI for the economy and national security, and the countries that lead in AI will shape it and get the most from it in the short and long run,” the AWS CEO wrote.

“The choices we make today will determine that outcome, and a lapse in our nation’s focus or resolve could put us behind, and potentially irreparably so,” he added.

data.title: $2.5 billion Amazon settlement: More payments being sent out, with another round possible
data.description:
(NEXSTAR) – More — and larger — payments connected to a $2.5 billion settlement Amazon reached with the Federal Trade Commission last year may soon be available, according to officials.

The settlement came last year after Amazon was accused of using “deceptive methods” to register millions of customers for paid Prime subscriptions, then making it difficult for those customers to cancel. Amazon did not admit wrongdoing.

Of the $2.5 billion involved in the settlement, $1.5 billion was to be used on customer refunds.

Some impacted consumers received automatic payments late last year as part of the agreement. Another group had to complete a claims process. At the time, the FTC said payments were capped at $51, but could be less than $1.

Now, following a joint motion from the FTC and Amazon, “millions” more are now eligible for automatic payouts, and another round of payments may be sent out.

More consumers now qualify for payment, FTC says

Part of the original qualifications was that you had to have used fewer than 10 Prime benefits during a one-year period after becoming a member. Now, the FTC says automatic payments will be provided to “millions of additional consumers who used between 11 and 20 Prime benefits during a one-year period.”

You still need to have either signed up for Prime with Amazon’s “challenged enrollment flow” (including signing up through the universal Prime decision page, shipping selection page, single page checkout, or the Prime Video enrollment flow) or tried but failed to cancel your U.S. subscription. Either needs to have happened between June 23, 2019, and June 23, 2025.

Amazon was expected to start sending funds via Venmo, PayPal, or a check in the mail to members of this group on Thursday.

Additionally, if you were notified that you qualified for this settlement, but did not file a claim before the July deadline, you may instead receive an automatic payment from Amazon if you are deemed eligible.

Payments may increase to $200 maximum

As part of the joint motion, the payment cap may adjust from $51 to $200. That means those who received a $51 payment may see another totaling up to $149.

You do not need to do anything to receive this second round of payments, according to settlement administrators.

It’s not yet clear whether these additional payments will actually be sent out, though. It will come down to whether the “consumer-accepted payments … reach the required threshold by February 2027,” according to the FTC. As of September, Amazon had distributed more than $845 million, but less than the $1.5 billion it was required to pay in redress.

You have 30 days to accept a digital payment to receive the funds, or 60 days to cash a check, if you opt for that method. You can find more details on the settlement website, including instructions on what to do if you are unable to redeem your payment.

Should another round of payments happen, the FTC said it will start by April 2027 and distribution will happen automatically.

data.title: Hegseth announces all US troops will get one day off to vote in October
data.description:
Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced on Friday that all U.S. troops will get one day off in October to vote in the 2026 midterm elections.

Hegseth said the stand-down order will be executed by Oct. 15 and will continue in even-numbered election years as part of a new and “apolitical” Pentagon “with all the right priorities.” 

“Under the leadership of President Trump, we’re upholding things that are central to the defense of our republic and our American way of life, and we’re doing this because in the past voting for our men and women in uniform has been time-consuming and complex, as many warriors reside outside of their home state for obvious reasons,” Hegseth said in a two-and-a-half-minute video posted on social platform X. 

“They face unnecessary, difficult ways of obtaining, completing and returning absentee ballots while serving far from home,” he added. 

The stand-down order will ensure service member training, processing and submission of the Federal Post Card Applications (FPCA) if service members decide to vote by absentee ballot, Hegseth in a Thursday memo.

The announcement comes a week after the Defense secretary urged U.S. service members and their families to register and vote in the 2026 midterms, stating that about 300,000 troops did not register to cast votes two years ago. 

“Regardless of your home state or current duty status, you can use a standardized federal postcard to register and request a ballot, and if you’re forward deployed and your standard ballot is delayed, you can use the federal write-in absentee ballot,” Hegseth said Sept. 25. “All of these processes are straightforward and protected by law,”

Just like last week, Hegseth emphasized that he is not telling service members for whom they should to cast their ballots. 

“Now we’re not telling you who to vote for, but we will give you every opportunity to do so. It’s then up to you to exercise your right as an American to choose your elected leaders,” Hegseth said in the video. 

Around two-thirds of active-duty military members were registered to vote in the 2024 election, a 3-point decrease compared to 2020, according to Federal Voting Assistance Program (FVAP) data. 

“Voting is the way our founding fathers envisioned every citizen’s ability to participate in government,” Hegseth said. “We’re going to take the time to ensure that you can vote and that your voice is heard.”

data.title: Cornell survey finds 35 percent of female undergrads reported nonconsensual sexual contact in 2025
data.description:
Over 35 percent of undergraduate women at Cornell University reported experiencing nonconsensual sexual contact during their time at the Ivy League institution in 2025, according to a poll conducted by the university. 

The survey results have gained renewed attention following fresh scrutiny over a 2024 allegation of sexual assault on Cornell’s campus. 

In a new lawsuit filed last month, the woman, identified as Jane Doe, said she was drugged and gang raped by seven men at the Chi Phi fraternity house. She initially reported the incident to campus police three weeks after the alleged assault occurred on Oct. 15, 2024. 

The 2025 Cornell Survey of Sexual Assault and Related Misconduct was conducted among 926 undergraduate, graduate and professional students in the spring semester of 2025.

Reports of sexual assault were higher among women involved in Greek life at Cornell in the survey, with 52 percent of this population reporting experiencing nonconsensual sexual contact, compared to 29 percent of respondents who were not Greek-affiliated. About 8 percent of all undergraduate men reported experiencing a sexual assault while enrolled at the university, according to the poll.

A 2023 survey found 23 percent of Cornell’s female undergraduate population reported being sexually assaulted while enrolled, compared to 20 percent of this same population in 2021. 

Additionally, the 2025 data shows 29 percent of reported sexual assaults occurred in residence halls, followed by 23 percent at off-campus residences and 17 percent at fraternity chapter houses. 

Prosecutors in New York state reopened an investigation into the 2024 allegation of gang rape on Cornell’s campus this week amid outrage from state leaders and federal lawmakers with the original probe into this incident. 

On Thursday, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul (D) appointed state Attorney General Letitia James (D) as special prosecutor to lead the criminal investigation. 

Hochul told reporters during a Friday morning press conference she was “deeply disturbed” by how Cornell University’s police department handled the case, citing the “partial record” the office shared with the Tompkins District Attorney’s Office. She stopped short, however of calling for District Attorney Matthew Van Houten or the university’s president to step down.

The governor did, however, criticize Van Houten’s decision not to interview the woman who brought the statement or bring criminal charges in this case. 

“New reporting raises serious questions about the information his office relied upon when it made that decision, and that’s why I believe this case demands a special prosecutor who will provide a fresh and thorough review of all the facts, including the information that has recently come to light,” Hochul said.

data.title: If America wants to prosper, we must lead
data.description:
Last week at the United Nations General Assembly, President Trump issued a “challenge for every nation in this room” to “go forward strong and united against the enemies of all humanity” and, by doing so, “make this world a far better and safer place.” While it is tempting to write Trump’s words off as rhetorical fanfare, the mission they describe is real, critical and — unfortunately — now being dismissed by many in the U.S.

Lately, a foolish worldview is growing in popularity among elected leaders in Washington. You hear it from voices ranging from Tucker Carlson to Hasan Piker. Some on the left and right have become convinced that solving America’s domestic issues requires our retreat from leadership on the world stage.

Their narrative requires us to ignore history and believe that America is in irreversible decline and has shriveled in form from her former greatness. But America’s best days are ahead, and we can and must stay energetically engaged in foreign policy to protect Americans and our way of life. And so, we must be clear about what a U.S. retreat would mean and how American life would look if we allowed Communist China to write the rules and our enemies to establish a New World Order.

These views, often sold as populist ideas, are nothing new. Nearly a century ago, America faced similar choices as evil around the world began to threaten our security.

In the fall of 1939, the devastation caused by the Great Depression hung like a dark cloud over the lives of many Americans while Nazi Germany invaded Poland. While the news out of Europe was troubling, there were plenty of “leaders” in Washington telling hardworking families that America couldn’t possibly be worried about the security of Europe when our own citizens couldn’t guarantee the security of their own jobs.

These are the same arguments being sold today as young Americans worry about grocery bills, the cost of electricity, and how they are going to afford to raise a family. Of course, the choice between global leadership and domestic prosperity is a false one.

The American Dream depends on the United States’ leadership in the world, where we set rules in a way that protects the American people, secures our economy, and advances our goals.

America First is not possible if America surrenders its position on the world stage. We want an America strong enough to deter our enemies and win a war if an adversary starts one. That does not mean getting entangled in forever wars and needless regime change operations with no goal and no endgame.

What the Tucker-Piker camp fails to understand is that America still has enemies. Communist China, Russia, Iran, North Korea, and Cuba have created an anti-American coalition — an authoritarian alliance — to undercut us as the global superpower and sever the ties between the U.S. and the Western coalition.

And it doesn’t end with China — Russia is waging a war of choice in Ukraine to test the resolve of NATO and to scare Americans into believing that they must surrender peace among their oldest and most prosperous Western democracies or risk catastrophic war.

Those powers — supported by authoritarians in Iran, North Korea and Cuba — are consolidating with one goal: undermine the United States, replace its influence with those of authoritarian powers, and undermine the world that the West has built.

This is happening at different levels and with different methods. The Chinese Communist Party is leveraging economic dependence against the West to bend our allies toward its interests. Russia is attempting to break NATO to claim territory from sovereign democratic nations. Iran is destabilizing the Middle East and global trade. Meanwhile, North Korea is investing in its illegal nuclear missile program while providing soldiers to Russia for its war against Ukraine.

All four nations are collaborating in various ways, and aim to push the U.S., its forward deployed bases, and its influence out of their regions. In our own, Cuba has proven to be the greatest destabilizing force in the Western Hemisphere for decades.

I have no doubt our foreign adversaries see a useful domestic asset in Islamist-Socialist Hasan Piker — an American via birthright citizenship only — who wants capitalists dead, believed 9/11 was justified, and campaigns for socialists in our elections.

It cannot be any clearer: the authoritarian alliance desires the destruction of the postwar order, and the rights and prosperity generations have died defending.

If we retreat and allow this authoritarian alliance to take hold, America will suffer. Communist China and its accomplices will starve us, isolate us, and deprive us of every resource possible until America is weak and dependent. We will have no autonomy, no opportunity, and no freedom. Our financial markets will be powerless to fuel innovation, our business will shutter, and the American Dream will die.

President Trump and Secretary of State Marco Rubio understand what’s at stake, and they’ve shown that there’s a smarter way to do it than the mistakes we’ve seen this century. They showed the world America is not giving up. President Trump made NATO allies recommit to the alliance and have encouraged others outside the alliance to join the cause.

They also understand the need to reduce our exposure to our enemies, especially via trade. Every dollar we send to Beijing — and the rest of the authoritarian alliance — is capital for them to hurt us and our allies.

Retreating from the challenges to our power will not appease them; it only increases the cost of confronting them down the road. Strong leadership creates the environment for domestic security and economic prosperity. Without it, America and her allies remain vulnerable to criminal regimes who hate our way of life.

We cannot sacrifice national and global security to a false dilemma of domestic versus overseas issues. It is not a zero-sum equation. To believe it would destroy a century of American greatness and the American Dream itself.

Americans deserve a future that is safe, prosperous and free. For that to happen, America must lead.

Rick Scott is Florida’s senior U.S. senator. He serves on the Foreign Relations and Armed Services committees. Rebeccah Heinrichs is a senior fellow at Hudson Institute and the director of its Keystone Defense Initiative.
